subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When reading an Ordnance Survey grid reference, which coordinate is always given first?
questions.explain: You read the eastings first ('along the corridor') and then the northings ('up the stairs').

questions.q: A four-figure grid reference identifies which of the following on an OS map?
options: A single point to the nearest 100 m
questions.explain: A four-figure reference locates the whole 1 km grid square, while six figures pinpoint a location within it.

questions.q: Why is a six-figure grid reference more precise than a four-figure reference?
options: It divides each 1 km square into tenths (100 m intervals)
It uses latitude and longitude instead of the grid
It measures the height of the land
It gives the map scale as well as the location
questions.explain: Imagining each 1 km square split into tenths lets a six-figure reference locate a point to about 100 m.

questions.q: On an Ordnance Survey map, contour lines join points of equal:
questions.explain: Contour lines connect points at the same height above sea level.

questions.q: Contour lines drawn very close together on a map indicate:
questions.explain: Closely spaced contours mean height changes over a short distance, so the gradient is steep.

questions.q: On a 1:25 000 OS map, two points are 6 cm apart. What is the real distance on the ground?
questions.explain: At 1:25 000, 1 cm represents 0.25 km, so 6 cm represents 6 x 0.25 = 1.5 km.

questions.q: Bearings are measured in degrees clockwise from which direction?
questions.explain: A bearing is measured clockwise from north, giving a value between 0 and 360 degrees.

questions.q: Which mapping technique represents data by shading whole areas according to their value or density?
questions.explain: A choropleth map uses graded shading, with darker shades usually showing higher values.

questions.q: Which type of map uses lines to join places of equal value, such as height or temperature?
questions.explain: An isoline map joins points of equal value with lines, as contour lines do for height.

questions.q: On a climate graph, how are precipitation and temperature usually shown?
options: Precipitation as bars and temperature as a line
Precipitation as a line and temperature as bars
questions.explain: Climate graphs plot monthly precipitation as bars and monthly temperature as a line.

questions.q: A population pyramid is used to show a population's:
questions.explain: A population pyramid displays the proportion of males and females in each age group.

questions.q: A scatter graph is most useful for showing:
options: Change in one value over time only
The age structure of a population
questions.explain: Scatter graphs plot paired data to reveal whether two variables are correlated.

questions.q: On a triangular graph, the three plotted values must always add up to:
questions.explain: Triangular graphs plot three proportions that together must total 100%.

questions.q: Which graph is the most suitable choice for showing the proportions of a whole as segments of a circle?
questions.explain: A pie chart divides a circle into segments to show each category's share of the total.

questions.q: A pie chart represents 200 people. What angle should be used to show a group of 50 people?
questions.explain: The angle is (50 / 200) x 360 = 90 degrees.

questions.q: A negative correlation on a scatter graph means that as one variable increases, the other:
questions.explain: In a negative correlation the two variables move in opposite directions.

questions.q: How is the mean of a data set calculated?
options: Add all the values and divide by the number of values
Take the middle value when ordered
Subtract the smallest value from the largest
questions.explain: The mean is the total of all values divided by how many values there are.

questions.q: The mode of a data set is:
options: The difference between the highest and lowest values
The sum divided by the number of values
questions.explain: The mode is the value that appears most often in the data set.

questions.q: What is the median of the data set: 3, 7, 4, 9, 6?
questions.explain: Ordered, the values are 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, and the middle value is 6.

questions.q: A town's population rises from 4000 to 5000. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explain: Percentage change is (1000 / 4000) x 100 = 25%.
